title: Milestone number rolls up one step at a time
summary: A big accent-coloured number on white ticks up one unit at a time, each digit rolling upward through a clip, then cascades into the round milestone while a short label rises in below. Built-in suspense, one clear figure.
use_when: Announcing a round milestone (users, downloads, stars)
A short silent social post where one number is the whole message
A stat insert inside a longer launch film
A growth update that should feel earned, not shouted

look.type_style: heavy rounded grotesk numerals, tabular, tight tracking, ~20 % of frame height, accent blue with a soft same-hue drop shadow; label bold grotesk, sentence case, black, ~6 % H, centred under the number

structure.shot: one shot: a three-digit number centred on white steps up twice by one, then rolls to the round four-digit milestone; a 3-word label rises in below and holds
structure.camera: locked-off frame, no camera move; the number group re-centres as it widens from 3 to 4 digits plus separator at ~1.50 (±0.25 s)
structure.motion: counter steps every ~0.75 s (22 fr, ±0.25 s): changing digit rolls up through a clip mask, old digit exits up, new one enters from below, springs.ui ~15 fr (overshoot not measurable); step 1 in progress at f0, settled by f15; step 2 starts ~f23, settled by f38; final step ~f40: all digits roll together with a ~2 fr per-digit stagger (±0.25 s), leading digit and separator enter, group re-centres, settled ~f55-60; label words mask-rise from f50, stagger ~4 fr (±0.25 s), springs.ui, settled by f68; hold f68-f90

params.target: the milestone number the count lands on (round number reads best)
params.steps: how many single-unit steps before the milestone (reference: 3, one every ~22 fr)
params.label: what the number counts, 2-4 words, sentence case

notes: Measured from one 4 fps sheet (0.25 s resolution) plus keyframes at 0.50/1.50/2.50 s; no cuts, silent. Count advances by single units with holds (proposed term: step-roll), not a continuous ticker. motion.json reports ~8.7 %/s zoom in the first 2 s; the unchanged digits keep their size and position across cells, so it is read as the digit rolls and the final widening, not a camera move. Sfx planned by the glue rule, not measured.
